what: evidence behind two stand-method rules added to benchmark/README.md on 2026-10-02
experiment: ASD-STE100 borrows, epoch ste1 (a separate stand clone, not the shipped harness)
part1_rule: identical text: e16-noiseband, 12 tasks (D01 D02 D03 D05 D06 D07 D08 D09 D10 D13 D14 D15), 4 runs per task split 2+2 at random, 20000 draws per seed; share of draws where the candidate's median (bar A) or total (bar B) turn-1 words exceed 1.15 x the base's
word_unit: a whitespace-separated token of turn 1's result text (the agent's first reply), as harness ste_measure.py counts it
design_note: measured on the experiment's 12-task design (2 runs per arm per task); the sibling comparison that first used the bar had 4 tasks

built_by.script: work/evidence_method.py in the experiment folder ~/Desktop/PayneBenchmark/ste-2026-10-02 (not shipped)

part2_rule: a mutant = ste_compare.py with one constant changed or one check removed; CAUGHT when the worked values exit 1; FAR = the first 8 registered cases, EDGE = the full test_ste_compare.py with boundary cases
part2_note: five mutants change a constant, the sixth removes the base answered-count check; on these inputs the rule's unequal-runs check sends that case to the human anyway
part3_rule: epoch ste1 (claude-sonnet-5, tasks5 D01 D02 D03 D05 D06 D07 D08 D09 D10 D13 D14 D15, 2 runs per arm per task, 2 turns), each candidate against rlp0 (0.9.8 + the human's plain-language block) by the reading rule registered in the experiment's own decision log before launch: discipline dims >= base - k (k from part 1's null), total turn-1 words <= 1.15 x base, for steQ/steDg median sentence length <= 0.85 x base; steP = rewritten AGENT.md + glossary + warning shape, steQ = steP + STE lines in the block, steDg = rewritten digest + STE block. NOT in one epoch for every task: the base's D01 D02 D03 D05 cells (8 of its 24 runs) were reused from epoch e29 of the same day (same model, same payload 99a0edc3), so those four tasks — the D02 consent slips of steP included — compare across epochs, which this repo's own methodology says can only estimate a band

part3_definitions.model: claude-sonnet-5 (pinned; the e16 null of part 1 ran on the same model)
part3_definitions.dims: the stand scorer's per-run booleans (harness scoring.py 812d63e0); x/n = runs scored True / runs the task measures
part3_definitions.k_rule: smallest k with P(candidate - base < -k) <= 0.05 per measure on part 1's null split 2+2; the score measures alone false-alarm at 0.0405 (seed 11, 20000 draws) — the whole no-harm rule is in whole_rule_rate below; claim_sourced is report-only (k >= its runs), contradiction_flagged report-only by the human's choice; a miss resting on one run of a k=0 measure goes to the human
part3_definitions.words_total: sum over the arm's 24 answered runs of turn-1 words (word_unit above)
part3_definitions.sentence_median: median over runs of each run's median words per sentence in turn 1's final text, by the pinned splitter scripts/ste_sentences.py (sentences under 3 words dropped)
part3_definitions.share_sentences_le20: share of all turn-1 sentences of the arm with 20 words or fewer, same splitter
part3_definitions.warning_lines: lines starting with the warning sign in the final texts of turns 1 and 2, summed over 24 runs
part3_definitions.in_tokens_median_per_run: median over runs of input + cache-read + cache-creation tokens of the main agent, both turns, from the result events

whole_rule_rate.rule: identical text, 2+2 split: any decisive score measure below base - k, or total turn-1 words above 1.15 x base (the benefit bar not included: it points the other way)
